```{r setup, include=FALSE}
required_packages <- c("data.table", "ggplot2", "stabledist", "tea", "knitr")
missing <- required_packages[!vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing)) stop("Install required R packages: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center", dpi = 140)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "-")
show_table <- function(z, title, digits = NULL) {
  if (nrow(z) == 0L) {
    cat(paste0("**", title, ":** no rows under the current rules.\n\n"))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  # Keep automatic escaping of the data (e.g. AKT2_5), while displaying
  # mathematical symbols only in headings after knitr has escaped text.
  math_headings <- c(
    alpha_hat = "$\\widehat{\\alpha}$",
    alpha_dAMSE = "$\\widehat{\\alpha}_{\\mathrm{dAMSE}}$",
    alpha_Hill_reexam = "$\\widehat{\\alpha}_{\\mathrm{Hill,reexam}}$",
    alpha_L_reexam = "$\\widehat{\\alpha}_{L,\\mathrm{reexam}}$",
    alpha_L = "$\\widehat{\\alpha}_{L}$",
    alpha = "$\\widehat{\\alpha}$"
  )
  original_cols <- names(z)
  renamed_cols <- original_cols
  for (j in seq_along(original_cols)) {
    if (original_cols[j] %in% names(math_headings))
      renamed_cols[j] <- paste0("MATHHEADER", j, "END")
  }
  args <- list(
    x = z,
    col.names = renamed_cols,
    format = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "latex" else "pipe",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    # kable() leaves LaTeX captions unescaped. Guide names such as AKT2_5
    # would otherwise trigger "Missing $ inserted" during PDF compilation.
    caption = if (knitr::is_latex_output())
      gsub("_", "\\\\_", title) else title,
    longtable = knitr::is_latex_output() && nrow(z) > 25L,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  if (!is.null(digits) && length(digits) > 0L) {
    args$digits <- digits
  }

  rendered <- as.character(do.call(knitr::kable, args))
  for (j in seq_along(original_cols)) {
    if (original_cols[j] %in% names(math_headings)) {
      placeholder <- paste0("MATHHEADER", j, "END")
      # strsplit/paste preserves literal LaTeX backslashes in the replacement.
      rendered <- vapply(strsplit(rendered, placeholder, fixed = TRUE),
                         paste, collapse = math_headings[[original_cols[j]]],
                         FUN.VALUE = character(1))
    }
  }
  cat(paste(rendered, collapse = "\n"), "\n\n", sep = "")
  invisible(NULL)
}
fmt_ci <- function(l, u, digits = 3L) {
  ifelse(is.finite(l) & is.finite(u),
         sprintf(paste0("[%.", digits, "f, %.", digits, "f]"), l, u), "-")
}

# Processes: Eirew et al. and the SRM adaptation

```{r workflow, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=6, fig.cap="Comparison of the original approach of Eirew et al. (2022) and the SRM application. The two estimands are not identical."}

              "Normalized SRM fitness + Eirew comparison"))
))
workflow[, fill := ifelse(x < 0, "#DCEAF8", "#DFEEDC")]

ggplot() +

           label = c("Eirew et al. (2022)", "SRM adaptation"),

           label = "I_t is an initial read count, not the number of initial clones. No artificial zeros.",
           size = 2.65, colour = "firebrick") +
  scale_fill_identity() + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-3.7,3.7), ylim = c(-.1,7.95), clip = "off") +
  theme_void() -> p_workflow

ggsave(file.path("figures_thesis", "ch4_workflow_comparison.pdf"), p_workflow,
       width = 6.5, height = 6)
p_workflow
```

Only gene-targeting sgRNAs are analysed. Control sgRNAs are excluded before
estimating the tail index or running O'Brien, Hill and SRM. The observed clone
size is denoted by $M$; $S_t$ remains the number of positive barcodes and
is retained in the normalization formula because $S_t$ and $M$ are different quantities.

The **SRM target** for sgRNA $t$ is the conditional mean $\mu_t^+=E[M_t\mid M_t>0]$ of the *unwinsorized* positive counts. Eirew et al. model a **winsorized** mean cellular output (also accounting for unobserved extinction) and report its normalized posterior median and 95% credible interval. Therefore the final fitness comparison is **descriptive** rather than an equivalence of estimands or an accuracy comparison.

# Step 1 -- dAMSE estimates of $\alpha$

```{r tail-estimation, include=FALSE}
damse_one <- function(x) {
  empty <- list(tail_status="failed", alpha_damse=NA_real_, k_damse=NA_integer_,
                threshold_damse=NA_real_)
  if (length(x)<minimum_tail_n || uniqueN(x)<minimum_distinct) {
    empty$tail_status <- "insufficient_data"; return(empty)
  }
  fit <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(tea::dAMSE(x)), error=function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(fit)) return(empty)
  a <- as.numeric(fit$tail.index)[1L]
  k <- as.integer(fit$k0)[1L]
  threshold <- as.numeric(fit$threshold)[1L]
  if (length(a)!=1 || !is.finite(a) || a<=0 || length(k)!=1 || is.na(k) ||
      k<2 || k>=length(x) || length(threshold)!=1 ||
      !is.finite(threshold) || threshold<=0) return(empty)
  list(tail_status="ok",alpha_damse=a,k_damse=k,threshold_damse=threshold)
}
tail <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(summary)), function(i) {
  g <- summary$sgRNA_index[i]
  z <- damse_one(raw[sgRNA_index==g,M])
  data.table(sgRNA_index=g, tail_status=z$tail_status,
             alpha_damse=z$alpha_damse,k_damse=z$k_damse,
             threshold_damse=z$threshold_damse)
}))
summary <- merge(summary,tail,by="sgRNA_index",all.x=TRUE,sort=FALSE)
summary[, damse_candidate := tail_status=="ok" & alpha_damse>1]
summary[, alpha_lower_damse := fifelse(damse_candidate,
  alpha_damse-alpha_z*alpha_damse/sqrt(k_damse), NA_real_)]
fwrite(summary[, .(sgRNA_index,sgRNA_official,gene,S_t,alpha_damse,
                    k_damse,threshold_damse,alpha_lower_damse,damse_candidate)],
       file.path(results_dir,"01_all_dAMSE.csv"))
```

The approximate one-sided 95% lower confidence bound for the upper-tail
exponent is calculated as

$$
\widehat{\alpha}_{L,t}
= \widehat{\alpha}_{t}
- 1.645\,\frac{\widehat{\alpha}_{t}}{\sqrt{k_t^*}},
$$

where $\widehat{\alpha}_{t}$ is the dAMSE estimate and $k_t^*$ is its
selected number of upper-tail observations. We retain in Table 2 **only**
sgRNAs with $\widehat{\alpha}_{L,t}>1$. The SRM construction for the mean
requires a moment order satisfying $1<p<q<\alpha_t$. If the estimated lower
bound is at most 1, no $p>1$ satisfies our conservative selection rule.
This lower bound is an **approximate Hill-type screening criterion**, not
proof that the mean exists or a confidence bound with guaranteed 95% coverage
after dAMSE's data-driven choice of $k_t^*$.

```{r damse-table, results='asis'}
show_table(summary[
  damse_candidate == TRUE &
  is.finite(alpha_lower_damse) & alpha_lower_damse > 1
][order(-alpha_damse),
  .(sgRNA=sgRNA_official,
    alpha_hat=round(alpha_damse,3),
    alpha_L=round(alpha_lower_damse,3))],
  "sgRNAs retained by dAMSE with lower tail-index bound above 1")
```

# Step 2 -- O'Brien for $\widehat{\alpha}_{\mathrm{dAMSE}}\leq 1$, and Hill-plot re-examination

We apply O'Brien **only** when dAMSE gives $\widehat{\alpha}\leq1$ (including the boundary). A decreasing permutation-averaged maximum-to-sum ratio is evidence worth investigating, **not proof** that a moment exists. A flat curve does **not prove** that the mean is infinite. All Pareto, O'Brien, Hill and running-mean plots are kept in the separate diagnostic appendix.

```{r obrien-and-hill-functions, include=FALSE}
# Supervisor's method: regression of the mean of LOG(max/sum) over
# 40 random permutations and 60 log-spaced prefix sizes, from 50 to n.
obrien_one <- function(x, seed, B=40L, grid_points=60L) {
  if(length(x)<50L) return(list(status="unavailable",slope=NA_real_,
       neg_share=NA_real_,curve=data.table()))
  set.seed(seed)
  fit <- tryCatch(obrien_slope(x,n_points=grid_points,n_perm=B),
                  error=function(e) NULL)
  if(is.null(fit)) return(list(status="unavailable",slope=NA_real_,
                              neg_share=NA_real_,curve=data.table()))
  slope <- as.numeric(fit$slope)
  status <- if (is.finite(slope) && slope < obrien_slope_cutoff)
              "decreasing" else "not_clearly_decreasing"
  # Convert mean log ratio back to a geometric-mean ratio only for plotting.
  # The classification is calculated on mean(log(M/S)), not on log(mean(M/S)).
  # The supervisor's original obrien_slope() returns only slope,
  # avg_logratio and idx. The extended variant also returns logratio_mat
  # and permutation_slopes. Reconstruct the SAME permutation sample (using
  # the seed above) when those optional outputs are absent.
  idx <- as.integer(fit$idx)
  logmat <- fit$logratio_mat
  if (!is.matrix(logmat) || ncol(logmat) != length(idx) ||
      nrow(logmat) < 2L) {
    set.seed(seed)
    logmat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = B, ncol = length(idx))
    for (b in seq_len(B)) {
      xp <- sample(x)
      cs <- cumsum(abs(xp))
      cm <- cummax(abs(xp))
      logmat[b, ] <- log(cm[idx] / cs[idx])
    }
  }
  # Match the original definition: average log ratio before exponentiating.
  ratio_geo <- exp(colMeans(logmat))
  ratio_q10 <- exp(apply(logmat, 2L, quantile, probs = .10, na.rm = TRUE))
  ratio_q90 <- exp(apply(logmat, 2L, quantile, probs = .90, na.rm = TRUE))
  individual_slopes <- fit$permutation_slopes
  if (is.null(individual_slopes) ||
      length(individual_slopes) != nrow(logmat)) {
    individual_slopes <- apply(logmat, 1L, function(y) {
      unname(coef(lm(y ~ log(idx)))[2L])
    })
  }
  set.seed(seed+5479L)
  mn <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow=B,ncol=length(fit$idx))
  for(i in seq_len(B)) {
    y <- sample(x,length(x),replace=FALSE)
    mn[i,] <- cumsum(y)[fit$idx]/fit$idx
  }
  list(status=status,slope=slope,
       neg_share=mean(individual_slopes < 0, na.rm=TRUE),
       curve=data.table(k=idx, ratio_mean=ratio_geo,
          ratio_q10=ratio_q10, ratio_q90=ratio_q90,
          running_mean=colMeans(mn),
          running_q10=apply(mn,2,quantile,probs=.10,na.rm=TRUE),
          running_q90=apply(mn,2,quantile,probs=.90,na.rm=TRUE)))
}

hill_profile_one <- function(x) {
  n <- length(x)
  z <- sort(x,decreasing=TRUE)
  k_max <- min(n-1L, floor(.35*n))
  if (k_max<25L) return(data.table())
  kvals <- seq.int(15L,k_max)
  cslog <- cumsum(log(z))
  gamma <- (cslog[kvals]/kvals)-log(z[kvals+1L])
  data.table(k=kvals,threshold=z[kvals+1L],
             hill_alpha=ifelse(gamma>0,1/gamma,NA_real_))
}

# Objective *exploratory* stability choice, not an estimator with established
# post-selection coverage: do NOT choose k on the basis of alpha crossing 1.
hill_stability_refit <- function(profile) {
  valid <- copy(profile[is.finite(hill_alpha) & hill_alpha>0])
  if (nrow(valid)<11L) return(list(k=NA_integer_,alpha=NA_real_,score=NA_real_))
  width <- 11L
  candidates <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(valid)-width+1L),function(j) {
    win <- valid[j:(j+width-1L)]
    data.table(k=win$k[ceiling(width/2)],
      alpha=median(win$hill_alpha),
      score=sd(log(win$hill_alpha))+.1/sqrt(median(win$k)))
  }))
  best <- candidates[which.min(score)]
  list(k=as.integer(best$k),alpha=as.numeric(best$alpha),score=as.numeric(best$score))
}
```

```{r run-obrien-refit, include=FALSE}
obrien_ids <- summary[tail_status=="ok" & alpha_damse<=1,sgRNA_index]
obrien_items <- lapply(obrien_ids,function(id) {
  x <- raw[sgRNA_index==id,M]
  fit <- obrien_one(x,seed=base_seed+id,B=obrien_permutations,
                    grid_points=obrien_curve_points)
  pf <- hill_profile_one(x)
  h <- if (fit$status=="decreasing") hill_stability_refit(pf) else
    list(k=NA_integer_,alpha=NA_real_,score=NA_real_)
  list(result=data.table(sgRNA_index=id,obrien_status=fit$status,
                         obrien_slope=fit$slope,obrien_negative_fraction=fit$neg_share,
                         hill_refit_alpha=h$alpha,hill_refit_k=h$k,
                         hill_refit_score=h$score),
       curve=fit$curve, hill=pf)
})
obrien_table <- if (length(obrien_items)) rbindlist(lapply(obrien_items, `[[`,"result")) else
  data.table(sgRNA_index=integer(),obrien_status=character(),obrien_slope=numeric(),
             obrien_negative_fraction=numeric(),hill_refit_alpha=numeric(),
             hill_refit_k=integer(),hill_refit_score=numeric())
obrien_curves <- if(length(obrien_items)) rbindlist(lapply(seq_along(obrien_items),function(i) {
  c0 <- copy(obrien_items[[i]]$curve)
  if(!nrow(c0)) return(NULL)
  c0[,sgRNA_index:=obrien_ids[i]];c0
}),fill=TRUE) else data.table()
hill_profiles <- if(length(obrien_items)) rbindlist(lapply(seq_along(obrien_items),function(i) {
  c0 <- copy(obrien_items[[i]]$hill)
  if(!nrow(c0)) return(NULL)
  c0[,sgRNA_index:=obrien_ids[i]];c0
}),fill=TRUE) else data.table()
summary <- merge(summary,obrien_table,by="sgRNA_index",all.x=TRUE,sort=FALSE)
summary[, `:=`(hill_refit_lower = fifelse(is.finite(hill_refit_alpha) &
                     is.finite(hill_refit_k) & hill_refit_k>1,
             hill_refit_alpha-alpha_z*hill_refit_alpha/sqrt(hill_refit_k),NA_real_),
  selection_class=fcase(damse_candidate==TRUE,"dAMSE_primary",
    obrien_status=="decreasing","OBrien_conflict_reexamine",
    default="not_selected"))]
setorder(summary,sgRNA_index)
fwrite(summary, file.path(results_dir,"02_all_diagnostics_and_selection.csv"))
```

    selection_class=="OBrien_conflict_reexamine" &
    is.finite(hill_refit_lower) & hill_refit_lower>1
  ][order(-hill_refit_lower),
    .(sgRNA=sgRNA_official,
      alpha_dAMSE=round(alpha_damse,3),

For discordant sgRNAs, the Hill stability re-estimation is *exploratory*. Its bound reuses an idealized Hill standard error after data-driven selection of $k$ and cannot be treated as a validated 95% lower confidence bound. We label any corresponding SRM intervals **exploratory nominal intervals**, never confirmed 95% confidence intervals.

# Step 3 -- Choose $p$ using the lower bound for $\alpha$

The proposed bound, adapted from the supervisor's working note, is

$$\widehat{\alpha}_{L,t}=\widehat{\alpha}_t-1.645\,\widehat{\alpha}_t/\sqrt{k_t^*}.$$

It is a one-sided normal/Hill approximation, **not** an exact guarantee and **not** an automatically calibrated dAMSE interval. For the primary analysis, retain $1<p<q<\widehat{\alpha}_{L,t}$, where $q=(p+\widehat{\alpha}_{L,t})/2$. The tested values of $p$ follow a fixed grid from 1.05 to 1.95 with increments of 0.05. An sgRNA is excluded from the SRM calculations if **no grid value** satisfies the condition; we do not manufacture an off-grid fallback near 1. In particular, a lower bound at or below 1.05 yields no value of $p$ on the chosen grid.

```{r p-grid, include=FALSE}
selection <- rbindlist(list(
  summary[damse_candidate==TRUE &
          is.finite(alpha_lower_damse) & alpha_lower_damse>1,
    .(sgRNA_index,sgRNA_official,gene,source="primary_dAMSE",
      alpha_for_p=alpha_damse,k_for_p=k_damse,alpha_lower=alpha_lower_damse)],
  summary[selection_class=="OBrien_conflict_reexamine" &
            is.finite(hill_refit_lower) & hill_refit_lower>1 &
            include_exploratory_refits==TRUE,
    .(sgRNA_index,sgRNA_official,gene,source="exploratory_OBrien_Hill",
      alpha_for_p=hill_refit_alpha,k_for_p=hill_refit_k,
      alpha_lower=hill_refit_lower)]
),fill=TRUE)

make_p_grid <- function(one) {
  a <- one$alpha_lower
  if(!is.finite(a) || a<=1) return(NULL)
  possible <- p_candidates[p_candidates>1 & p_candidates<2 & p_candidates<a]
  # Stay on the requested fixed 0.05 grid even for borderline alpha_L.
  if (!length(possible)) return(NULL)
  qval <- (possible+a)/2
  z <- data.table(sgRNA_index=one$sgRNA_index,
    sgRNA_official=one$sgRNA_official,gene=one$gene,
    source=one$source,alpha_for_p=one$alpha_for_p,
    k_for_p=one$k_for_p,alpha_lower=a,p=possible,q=qval)
  z[1<p & p<2 & p<q & q<a]
}
pq_grid <- if(nrow(selection)) rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(selection)),
  function(i) make_p_grid(selection[i])),fill=TRUE) else data.table()
if(nrow(pq_grid)) setorder(pq_grid,sgRNA_official,p)
fwrite(if(nrow(selection)) selection else data.table(),
       file.path(results_dir,"03_tail_bounds_all_candidates.csv"))
fwrite(pq_grid,file.path(results_dir,"04_p_q_pairs.csv"))

# Step 4 -- Compute SRM intervals for each p

Only successful numerical intervals appear in the printed $p$-tables.
Failed runs remain recorded in the exported CSV for reproducibility.

We now **call the supervisor's `srm_ci.R` directly**. Its stable random
variables use `beta=0.5, gamma=1, delta=0, pm=0`, unlike the previous
working implementation (`beta=0, gamma=0.5, delta=1, pm=0`). This can change
the intervals substantially. For each admissible $(p,q)$, the auxiliary
$q$ is a **moment-existence constraint**; `srm_ci()` itself takes only $p$
and the moment order `qprime=1`. The code records both the raw interval and
its intersection with $[0,\infty)$.

```{r srm-functions, include=FALSE}
srm_one <- function(x,p,q,seed,alpha_bound) {
  if(!is.finite(p) || !is.finite(q) || !is.finite(alpha_bound) ||
     !(1<p && p<2 && p<q && q<alpha_bound))
    stop("Require 1 < p < 2 and p < q < alpha_lower.")
  f <- srm_ci(x, p=p, qprime=q_prime, alpha=.05,
              rl=r_lower,ru=r_upper,n0=n0,
              y_beta=stable_beta,y_gamma=stable_gamma,
              y_delta=stable_delta,y_pm=stable_pm,
              ybar_range=stable_window,max_tries=max_stable_draws,
              seed=seed)
  # The supervisor's original srm_ci.R returns estimate, L, U, Ybar,
  # and ci, but does NOT return 'centre' or 'y_draws'.  Do not use
  # f$centre directly: NULL is silently dropped as a data.table column.
  # Reconstruct the exact resampling centre from either CI endpoint:
  # ci_lower = centre - rate*U, ci_upper = centre - rate*L,
  # with rate = n^(1/p-1)/Ybar.  This is algebra, not a new estimator.
  needed <- c("ci", "L", "U", "Ybar")
  if (!all(needed %in% names(f)))
    stop("srm_ci.R is missing required outputs: ",
         paste(setdiff(needed, names(f)), collapse=", "))
  L <- unname(f$ci["lower"])
  U <- unname(f$ci["upper"])
  if (length(L)!=1L || length(U)!=1L ||
      !is.finite(L) || !is.finite(U) || L>U ||
      length(f$Ybar)!=1L || !is.finite(f$Ybar) || f$Ybar==0 ||
      length(f$L)!=1L || length(f$U)!=1L ||
      !is.finite(f$L) || !is.finite(f$U))
    stop("Invalid or missing numerical SRM outputs from srm_ci.R")
  rate <- length(x)^(1/p-1) / f$Ybar
  center_from_lower <- L + rate * f$U
  center_from_upper <- U + rate * f$L
  if (!is.finite(center_from_lower) || !is.finite(center_from_upper) ||
      abs(center_from_lower-center_from_upper) >
        1e-7 * max(1,abs(center_from_lower),abs(center_from_upper)))
    stop("SRM centre reconstruction is inconsistent with the two CI endpoints")
  center <- center_from_lower
  if (length(f$centre)==1L && is.finite(f$centre)) {
    if (abs(f$centre-center) > 1e-7*max(1,abs(center)))
      stop("srm_ci.R centre disagrees with its interval endpoints")
    center <- as.numeric(f$centre)
  }
  draws <- if (length(f$y_draws)==1L && is.finite(f$y_draws))
              as.integer(f$y_draws) else NA_integer_
  if(U<0) return(list(status="empty_positive_intersection",
                    center=center,L_raw=L,U_raw=U,
                    L=NA_real_,U=NA_real_,width=NA_real_,
                    Ybar=f$Ybar,draws=draws))
  Lpos <- max(L,0)
  list(status="ok",center=center,L_raw=L,U_raw=U,
       L=Lpos,U=U,width=U-Lpos,Ybar=f$Ybar,draws=draws)
}
```

```{r compute-srm, include=FALSE}
srm <- if(nrow(pq_grid)) rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(pq_grid)),function(i) {
  row <- pq_grid[i]
  x <- raw[sgRNA_index==row$sgRNA_index,M]
  seed <- base_seed+10000L*row$sgRNA_index+as.integer(round(10000*row$p))
  tryCatch({
    f <- srm_one(x,row$p,row$q,seed,row$alpha_lower)
    data.table(sgRNA_index=row$sgRNA_index,p=row$p,q=row$q,
      status=f$status,detail=NA_character_,srm_center=f$center,
      ci_lower_raw=f$L_raw,ci_upper_raw=f$U_raw,
      ci_lower=f$L,ci_upper=f$U,ci_length=f$width,
      y_bar=f$Ybar,y_draws=f$draws)
  },error=function(e) data.table(sgRNA_index=row$sgRNA_index,p=row$p,q=row$q,
      status="failed",detail=conditionMessage(e),srm_center=NA_real_,
      ci_lower_raw=NA_real_,ci_upper_raw=NA_real_,
      ci_lower=NA_real_,ci_upper=NA_real_,ci_length=NA_real_,
      y_bar=NA_real_,y_draws=NA_integer_))
}),fill=TRUE) else data.table(sgRNA_index=integer(),p=numeric(),q=numeric(),
       status=character(),detail=character(),srm_center=numeric(),
       ci_lower_raw=numeric(),ci_upper_raw=numeric(),ci_lower=numeric(),

```

For the exploratory O'Brien/Hill sgRNAs the displayed 95% **nominal** intervals have no demonstrated 95% coverage. The primary dAMSE-derived rows also rely on an approximate Hill-style bound for $\alpha$, not a verified post-selection confidence procedure.

Clipping to nonnegative values preserves **at least** the original coverage for a strictly positive target **if** the original confidence interval itself has valid 95% coverage: $\{\mu\in [L,U]\}=\{\mu\in[L,U]\cap[0,\infty)\}$ for $\mu>0$. It does **not** correct misspecified SRM assumptions, random $p$-selection or plug-in normalization uncertainty.

The observed length need not be monotone in $p$, especially with randomized stable draws. The original SRM paper studies the effect of $p$ under its own simulation settings; a comparison is therefore qualitative rather than a predicted monotone law.

# Step 6 -- Scale SRM results and compare fitness with Eirew

As in the supplied code, the fixed empirical reference is

$$c=Q_{0.70}\left\{\overline M_t^+S_t/I_t: t\ \text{targets a gene}\right\},$$

where $I_t$ is the initial read count of sgRNA $t$ (variable `J_t` in the code).

This reference uses **all 168 gene-targeting sgRNAs**, not only the sgRNAs retained for the SRM. We regard $c$ and $S_t/I_t$ as plug-in quantities; their uncertainty is not propagated.

```{r normalize-and-compare, include=FALSE}
c_ref <- as.numeric(quantile(summary[,output_per_initial_read],
                             probs=.70,names=FALSE,type=7))
if(!is.finite(c_ref)||c_ref<=0) stop("Invalid empirical 70th-percentile reference.")
if(nrow(srm)) srm[,`:=`(
  fitness_srm=srm_center*(S_t/J_t)/c_ref,
  fitness_srm_lower=ci_lower*(S_t/J_t)/c_ref,
  fitness_srm_upper=ci_upper*(S_t/J_t)/c_ref,
  fitness_srm_length=ci_length*(S_t/J_t)/c_ref)]

published0 <- fread(paper_file)
stopifnot(all(c("tumour","guide","median","CI95_lo","CI95_hi") %in% names(published0)))
published <- published0[trimws(as.character(tumour))==target_tumour,
  .(sgRNA_official=trimws(as.character(guide)),
    paper_median=as.numeric(median),
    paper_lower=as.numeric(CI95_lo),paper_upper=as.numeric(CI95_hi))]
if(!nrow(published)||anyDuplicated(published$sgRNA_official))
  stop("Missing or duplicate C0331-231 published guide names.")
if(nrow(srm)) {
  srm <- merge(srm,published,by="sgRNA_official",all.x=TRUE,sort=FALSE)
  srm[, paper_overlap := fifelse(status=="ok" &
    is.finite(paper_lower)&is.finite(paper_upper),
    pmax(fitness_srm_lower,paper_lower)<=pmin(fitness_srm_upper,paper_upper),NA)]
  setorder(srm,sgRNA_official,p)
}
fwrite(data.table(tumour=target_tumour,reference_c=c_ref,
   definition="Empirical Q70 of mean(M positive)*S/J among all targeting guides"),
   file.path(results_dir,"06_normalization_reference.csv"))
fwrite(srm,file.path(results_dir,"07_fitness_SRM_vs_Eirew_all_p.csv"))
state <- list(raw=raw,guide_summary=summary,obrien_curves=obrien_curves,
              hill_profiles=hill_profiles,srm=srm,normalizer=c_ref,

saveRDS(state,file.path(results_dir,"diagnostic_state.rds"))

# Interpretation and limitations

**Interpretation boundaries.** (1) O'Brien and Pareto slopes are finite-sample diagnostics, not moment-existence tests with guaranteed decisions. (2) A Hill bound obtained after searching for a stable threshold is exploratory. (3) SRM intervals for such refits are labeled nominal and are not claimed to have established 95% coverage. (4) Intersecting a valid CI with the known nonnegative parameter space does not reduce coverage. (5) The empirical normalizer is treated as fixed. (6) Eirew fits a winsorized Bayesian mean fitness; SRM targets the non-winsorized positive-clone mean, with a plug-in survival/read normalization. The intervals do not automatically target identical estimands.

**Separate appendix:** knit `C0331_231_SRM_diagnostic_appendix.Rmd` *after* knitting this file; it reads `C0331_231_SRM_revised_results/diagnostic_state.rds`.

# References

- Das, A., Denker, M., Levina, A., and Tabacu, L. (2023). *Estimation by stable motions and its applications*. Probability and Mathematical Statistics, 43, 23--39.
- Eirew, P. et al. (2022). *Accurate determination of CRISPR-mediated gene fitness in transplantable tumours*. Nature Communications, 13, 4534. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-31830-2.
- Eirew et al., Supplementary Methods, especially Sections 1.1, 1.3, 1.5, and 1.6.
